markets.question: Will S&P 500 (SPX) hit $9,000 (HIGH) in December?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point between market creation and market close on the final day of trading for December 2026, any 1-minute candle for S&P 500 (SPX) shows a final "High" price equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

All prices recorded during regular trading hours of the primary exchange for the instrument, as reflected in Yahoo Finance's 1-minute interval ("1m") data, will be considered.

Periods when the market is officially closed (e.g., holidays or maintenance breaks) will not be considered.

All times referenced are local to the primary exchange on which the index trades.

The resolution source for this market is Yahoo Finance — specifically, the 1-minute interval ("1m") chart data for S&P 500 (SPX) available at https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EGSPC/.

eventMetadata.context_description: Strong second-quarter corporate earnings, with S&P 500 companies on pace for 33.5% year-over-year adjusted growth led by AI infrastructure spending, have lifted the index to recent records near 7,677 as of late August 2026, up roughly 12% year-to-date. Strategist consensus points to a median year-end 2026 target of 7,900, supported by rising earnings estimates and expectations that U.S.-Iran tensions ease. Persistent inflation, with headline PCE near 3.7%, has kept the Federal Reserve on hold at a 3.50-3.75% federal funds target range amid dissent for hikes, while upcoming catalysts including the July core PCE release, Nvidia results, and Jackson Hole speeches will shape near-term rate expectations and equity valuations.
